Sort animals into dead, review and alive bands

Source: R/detect_mortality.R
detect_mortality.Rd

Runs each rule stream of rules on the detection set and sorts every animal with a detection into the dead, review or alive band. The bands are a triage for the review cards of build_mortality_cards(): the call a person makes on a card is the verdict, and the rules never make it.

Usage

detect_mortality(x, rules = mortality_rules(), control = list())

Arguments

x

A detset.

rules

A list of rule streams from mortality_rules(), with any stream added by mortality_rule().

control

A list of options shared by the streams:

  • sites_km, the largest distance in km between two stations of one site (default 1); stations are clustered by complete linkage.

  • site_distance, NULL for straight-line distance, or a function of (lat, lon) that returns a square matrix of distances in km between the positions, such as in-water distances.

  • horizon, the end of the data as a POSIXct time in UTC; by default the last detection in x, of any transmitter. A horizon on a later date than the last detection in x, as for a month cut from a longer record, sets the tag-life comparison and the cards' days to the horizon, but record_end and site_listening still stop at the end of the detection record: x holds nothing after it, so an animal heard on its last day is cut off there, its end unknown, and goes to review with the end basis "end of the detection record". On a cut, death evidence that begins within within_days of the cut's end stays in review, whatever the horizon; a longer cut, or a smaller within_days in mortality_rules(), lets a final run reach the dead band.

  • sparse_to_review, TRUE (default) to send a record with too few detection days for the final run to the review band, or FALSE to leave it alive.

Value

An object of class mortality_bands, a list of:

  • bands: one row per animal with its band, the deciding rule and its label, the candidate death date and its basis, the persistence score, each stream's vote, and the statistics behind them.

  • votes: one row per animal and stream: rule, vote, score, date, basis and detail.

  • sensor: one row per sensor transmitter, with its accelerometer vote.

  • evidence: the rows behind the votes, one data frame per stream: the detection days of each final window, the daily sensor statistics and the persistence pairs.

  • sites: the station positions and their site.

  • settings: the options, the streams and counts used, and the detections and animals of x, which processing_report() and the cards use to log the step.

Details

The streams run in the order of rules, and each sees the votes of the streams before it, so movement after a candidate death date can be judged. The default streams are described in mortality_rules(). How the votes set the band:

  • dead: a death vote (an accelerometer flatline, or a terminal stationary run) with no alive vote, unless the death evidence begins within the record-end window of a record that ends near tag life or the data horizon, or the animal carries a sensor whose readings are not calibrated.

  • review: a death vote beside an alive vote (an active accelerometer, or movement after the candidate date); death evidence near the end of a record that ends near tag life or the horizon; a final run that is stationary across a site boundary, at one station whose recorded position moved, within near_factor times the site size, or at one site apart from stray detections on at most stray_days days; a record whose last site listened on less than listening_share of the within_days after its last detection, only when listening_share is set above its default of 0 (at the default the site_listening stream never votes and only reports the days on the cards); a record with no station position; a record too sparse for the final run; a persistence score at or above review_at; and a record with no death vote that ends near tag life or the horizon, because the rules cannot see what happened after it. A record with a death vote that ends there goes to review only when its death evidence begins within the record-end window (within_days of the record_end stream) of its last detection; evidence that begins earlier keeps the dead band, whatever record_end votes.

  • alive: no death evidence on a record that ends well before tag life and the horizon; with listening_share above 0, also at a site that kept listening.

The candidate death date. Only streams of kind "vote" give it: for an animal in the dead band, the date of the deciding stream's vote; for one in review, the earliest date of a dead or review vote. The final-run stream (terminal_run) dates a death by the first detection of the final stationary run. Where the site of the run listened on every day between the animal's detection before the run and the run's first detection, that date is the earliest the death could be given the detections: an animal may hold station alive at that site before it dies. Where the site did not listen on one or more of those days, the run may have started unheard. The date stays the first detection of the run, and its basis (death_date_basis, and on the card) counts the days the site was not listening and gives the date of the detection before the run as the earliest the death could be. A site listens on a day when a receiver at one of its stations is in the water and, after audit_listening(), not flagged as not listening. Evidence streams, such as depth_flatline, never set the date. Their records on the card are what the reviewer uses to date the death, and filter_mortality() cuts from the date of the call. The candidate date only guides the call.

Read the alive band for what it is. Because no record that ends near tag life or the horizon is put in the alive band, it holds only records that stopped early: animals that left the array, were harvested or eaten, or whose tags failed. Animals heard to the end of the study are never cleared without a card.

Inside the review band the persistence score ranks animals: the higher the score, the more stable the set of stations that heard the animal.

Accelerometers with raw readings only cast no vote, dead or alive, and detect_mortality() warns with their count. An animal that carries any sensor transmitter with raw readings only is never put in the dead band: its death evidence sends it to review under the rule uncalibrated_sensor, the column sensor_uncalibrated marks it, and a message names it, because the sensor it carries might have said alive.

The way votes combine into bands is this package's own rule; see mortality_rules() for the published kinds of evidence the streams read (Klinard and Matley 2020).

References

Klinard, N. V., and Matley, J. K. (2020). Living until proven dead: addressing mortality in acoustic telemetry research. Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries 30, 485-499. doi:10.1007/s11160-020-09613-z

See also

mortality_rules(), build_mortality_cards()

Examples

study <- example_mortality
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
# The defaults read final runs of 14 days; this study runs 2 to 10 June.
table(detect_mortality(dets)$bands$band)
#> 
#> review 
#>      4 
mort_rules <- mortality_rules(min_days = 3, min_calendar_days = 3,
                         min_flat_days = 2, within_days = 2)
bands <- detect_mortality(dets, rules = mort_rules)
bands
#> <mortality_bands> 4 animals in 20 sites of at most 1 km; streams:
#>   accel_flatline, terminal_run, depth_flatline, record_end, site_listening,
#>   movement_resumption, persistence
#>   dead      1 of 4 animals  (terminal_run 1)
#>   review    3 of 4 animals  (record_end 2; terminal_run_stray 1)
#>   alive     0 of 4 animals
#>   sensor streams: 2 rows; 0 accelerometers voted (0 dead, 0 alive)
#>   The bands are a triage. The call made on the review cards is the verdict.
table(bands$bands$band)
#> 
#>   dead review 
#>      1      3
